texto: To introduce yourself in Thai, the pronoun system offers several options depending on register, the relationship between speakers and social convention: «ผม» (phǒm, rising tone) is a formal polite pronoun in very wide use, while «ฉัน» (chǎn or chán, rising/high tone) and «ดิฉัน» (dì-chǎn, formal polite register) are common choices depending on how formal the situation is and on the speaker's preference. Still, in relaxed conversation it is very common to refer to yourself by your nickname or first name. The structure for giving your name is: [Pronoun] + «ชื่อ» (chʉ̂ʉ, to be called) + [Name].
